summary: Tested Provider-app onboarding (async job + poll) and internal entities (CRM contact panel + provider 'My Entities'), backend and frontend. Backend: 16/16 pytest pass. Checked: job running->done; result has pending_kyc, supabase_user_id, contact_id and welcome_email 'sent' for delivered@resend.dev; agent onboarding sets assigned_agent_id, type pharmacy, kyc pending, stage contacted and logs an activity; another staff user gets 404 on the job, master admin can see it; 400/422/403 validation; contact-entities access rules (admin and assigned agent allowed, Priya 403, unlinked contact 400, ambulance root 403, missing fields 400); create/delete entity; provider /api/provider/entities list/create/delete, staff token 403. Frontend: Contacts modal (5 optgroups, a form for each type, submit disabled until required fields + 10-digit phone + valid pincode, done screen shows 'Pending KYC approval' and the email message, Open contact navigates and the entities panel shows for the pharmacy contact). Agent Leads opens the new pa-onboard-modal and the ambulance-service picker returns results. Hospital contact as Rohan: entity add (ambulance with radius) and remove with confirm both work. Priya does not see the panel. Hospital provider login: 'My Entities' nav -> /provider/entities, add path_lab works and the API delete works. Onboardings made on prod Supabase: 2 pharmacies (TEST Pharmacy 3551 / 9184053551 by Rohan via API; TEST UI Pharmacy 0721 / 9240800721 by admin via UI). Every entity I created was removed.

minor.issue: Contact name comes from Supabase users.name, which is the person (ownerName/fullName), not the business. Pharmacy 'TEST UI Pharmacy 0721' was saved as contact 'TEST UI Owner'; the hospital contact d256e122 shows 'Test Admin'. The org name shown in the entities panel is also the person's name. Consider using businessName/name/labName/clinicName/bankName as the contact name and keeping the person as contact_person.

asyncio.create_task(run_job(...)) does not keep a reference to the task, so per the Python docs it can be garbage-collected mid-run. Store it in a module-level set. Jobs also stay 'running' forever if the backend restarts mid-job: no stale-job timeout.
Each call makes 2 upstream requests (by-admin + action), about 2.7s per GET, so a delete followed by a reload takes about 5-6s.

ui_bugs.issue: No busy state and no try/catch. After the confirm dialog nothing visible happens for about 5s (DELETE + reload), and a failed DELETE is an unhandled promise rejection with no message to the user. A first UI check 5s after confirm still showed the row; the API delete itself succeeded.

issues: Header overline shows 'PHARMACIE' and the AI card says 'Get instant context on this pharmacie'. typeLabel() strips the trailing 's' from 'Pharmacies'. Same kind of problem is likely for other '-ies' labels. Existing issue, not new in this change.

action_items: Use the business/organisation name (not the owner/admin name) as the contact name for onboarded organisations
Keep a reference to background onboarding tasks; add a stale-job timeout
EntitiesPanel: add a busy/disabled state and error handling to remove (and an optimistic update)
critical_code_review_comments: provider_onboard.py: find_one_and_update matches {$or:[supabase_user_id, phone]}. Onboarding a phone that already belongs to an unrelated contact (e.g. a patient) overwrites that contact's type and stage.
ContactDetail decides panel visibility from c.type in [hospital, pharmacy, pathologist, diagnostic_centre]; for any other contact type the backend returns 403 anyway, so the two are consistent.
PATCH entity route exists but has no UI (there is no edit entity option).
